name: replace-omission-clears: an unaddressed participant list, join link and highlight stay off the wire
description: The raw replace sends exactly what the caller passed, in one request, with no read-before-write. BC3 clears every writable field the body omits, EXCEPT the three named by this operation's preservedOnOmission carve-out (participant_ids, url, highlighted), which it seeds from the existing recordable. The SDK's job is narrow but load-bearing: when the caller says nothing about a carve-out, that key must not appear in the body at all. A compactor that emitted null, or a default that emitted [] or false, would clear the value the server is holding for us.

name: replace-clears-carve-outs: explicit empty values reach the wire
description: The counterpart to omission. An empty participant list means "remove everyone", an empty url means "drop the join link" and highlighted false means "stop highlighting" — each must be sent, because the server preserves what the request does not address. Ruby's compact_params and Python's _compact strip nil/None but not empty collections, empty strings or false, so this distinguishes "not addressed" from "addressed and cleared": the whole point of the BC3 guard.

name: replace-single-request: the raw path never reads before writing
description: SPEC section 18 rule 6: when a composite takes over the plain method name, the generated single-request method stays reachable under a name that says what it does — here `replace`, from the ReplaceScheduleEntry wire rename. This case exists so later generator drift cannot quietly turn both public methods into composite behavior. A full payload, and still exactly one PUT: no GET at index 0.

name: update-merge: a summary-only update preserves the times, description and all-day flag
description: The merge-safe update GETs the current entry, overlays only the explicitly-set fields, and PUTs the full representation back, so the four fields the caller never mentioned survive a full-replace endpoint. The read-back deliberately carries a populated join_url, highlighted and participants: none of the three may be echoed into the PUT. BC3 preserves them server-side, so resending them is redundant at best and wrong if the read raced a concurrent change — and echoing the response's `url` instead of `join_url` would write the entry's own API URL into its join link.

name: update-addresses-carve-outs: a caller-set join link and highlight reach the wire
description: Addressing a carve-out applies it normally. The caller's url goes on the wire under `url` — the request spelling — even though the response returns it as `join_url`. participant_ids stays absent, because this caller said nothing about participants, so the three carve-outs are independent rather than all-or-nothing.

name: update-clears-carve-outs: an explicitly empty join link, empty participant list and false highlight are sent
description: The falsey-value trap, on the composite this time. An empty string, an empty array and false are all "addressed and cleared" and must survive every SDK's body compaction — a `??`, `||` or `.compact` that treats them as absent would hand the clear back to BC3's carve-out, which preserves instead.

name: edit-clear: clearing the description keeps every other field
description: The read-modify-write closure seeds the entry's full writable state from the GET, the block mutates what it wants, and the whole representation is PUT back. Setting description empty clears it; summary, starts_at, ends_at and all_day ride through untouched.

name: edit-untouched-carve-outs: a block that never assigns them leaves them off the wire
description: The untouched half of the dirty-set contract. The GET returns a join link, a highlight and two participants; the block assigns only summary. None of the three carve-outs may appear in the PUT, so the edit view cannot simply serialize whatever it was seeded with.

name: edit-touched-carve-outs: assigning the value the read already returned still sends it
description: The touched half, and the reason the contract is setter-invocation dirty tracking rather than a snapshot diff. The block assigns exactly the join link and highlight the GET returned, so a value-comparison implementation would conclude nothing changed and omit both — handing the write back to BC3's carve-out. Intent is not recoverable from the value: `entry.url = entry.join_url` is a write, and this case fails for any SDK that decides otherwise.

name: create-join-link: url, highlighted and status reach the wire on create
description:
#641: BC3 has accepted `url`, `highlighted` and `status` on create since long before they were documented — `Schedules::Entries::BaseController#base_schedule_entry_params` permits the first two and `Recording::StatusParam#status_param` reads the third — but the SDK modelled none of them, so a caller wanting a video-call event with its join link had to create, read and replace through a non-atomic window, and `create` is the notifying write.

The write spelling is `url`, NOT `join_url`. `join_url` is read-only: `recordings/_recording` claims the `url` key for the recording's own API URL and the entry partial renders after it, so BC3 emits the join link under a non-colliding name on the way out. Strong parameters drop `join_url` on the way in, so sending it is a 201 with no join link — a silent no-op, which is why this case asserts its absence rather than only the presence of `url`.

Six runners, because the gap this closes was a hand-written one. The spec, the generated clients and five SDKs all carried these three while Go's public `CreateScheduleEntryRequest` did not, and nothing failed: every gate looked at the generated layer. A five-of-six that reads as six-of-six is what this case exists to catch.

name: create-omits-unset: an unset join link, highlight and status stay off the wire
description:
Unset means the key is absent, not a zero value on the wire. `highlighted` is the one that bites: `schedule_entries.highlighted` is NOT NULL, so an explicit `null` makes BC3 raise rather than apply its `false` default. `status` omitted means BC3's own default for an API create (`active`), and an omitted `url` means no join link.

This is the control for the case above: without it, a compactor that emitted all three unconditionally would still pass the presence assertions.
